title: The Score of a Balanced Word

concept.title: A stack of scores, one for every open level
body: The score of a balanced word of parentheses follows three rules: `()` has score 1; `AB` (two balanced words next to each other) has score `A + B`; `(A)` has score `2 * A`. This is a recursive definition, and recursion can be replaced by a **stack of scores**: the top of the stack is the score collected so far at the **current level**.

When `)` closes a level, the inner score is 0 for `()` (which counts 1) and `A` otherwise (which counts `2 * A`); `max(2 * inner, 1)` covers both. The score can be astronomically large for deep nesting, so it is printed modulo 1000000007 (take the modulo after every step).

statement: A balanced word of parentheses has a score: `()` has score 1, two balanced words `AB` next to each other have the score `A + B`, and `(A)` has the score `2 * A`. Print the score of the given word modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: A single balanced word of `(` and `)`.
hints: Keep a stack with the score of every level that is open.
On `(` push 0; on `)` pop the inner score and add `max(2 * inner, 1)` to the new top.

explanation: The stack keeps the score collected at every open level. Closing a level adds `max(2 * inner, 1)` to the level below.
